case.question: In a Spring application using the default proxy-based AOP, if a public method on a bean calls another method on the SAME bean that is annotated @Transactional, does a transaction start for that inner call? Explain why, and say what would make it work. Under 120 words.
case.expected_answer: No. In proxy mode only external calls through the proxy are intercepted, so self-invocation does NOT start a transaction even though the inner method is annotated. AspectJ mode (byte-code weaving, no proxy) would make it work; so would routing the call through the proxy.
case.source_quote: "In proxy mode (which is the default), only external method calls coming in through the proxy are intercepted. This means that self-invocation (in effect, a method within the target object calling another method of the target object) does not lead to an actual transaction at runtime even if the invoked method is marked with @Transactional." ... "Consider using AspectJ mode ... the target class is woven ... to support @Transactional runtime behavior on any kind of method."
case.wrong_answer_to_watch_for: Any claim that the transaction DOES start, or that making the inner method public is sufficient.

governed_answer:
No. Spring's default proxy-based AOP wraps the bean in a proxy that applies advice only when a call comes in through the proxy. A self-call (this.innerMethod()) is a direct call on the raw target object's internal reference, bypassing the proxy entirely, so the @Transactional interceptor never fires—no transaction starts (and no exception; it just silently runs non-transactionally). Fixes: move the method to a separate bean and call it via an injected reference (so the call goes through that bean's proxy); self-inject the bean's proxy (via ApplicationContext, AopContext.currentProxy() with exposeProxy=true, or @Lazy self-autowiring) and call through that reference; or switch to AspectJ compile-time/load-time weaving, which instruments bytecode directly and doesn't rely on proxies, so self-invocation works correctly.

B.verdict: No: the inner @Transactional call does not start a transaction because self-invocation bypasses the Spring AOP proxy.
B.answer: No. Default Spring AOP is proxy-based, so @Transactional advice runs only for calls that enter the bean through its Spring proxy. A same-bean call uses this and never hits the proxy, so no transaction interceptor runs and no transaction starts for the inner method. Route the call through the proxy to make it work: self-inject the bean and call the injected reference, use AopContext.currentProxy() with exposeProxy=true, move the annotated method to another bean, or switch to AspectJ compile-time or load-time weaving.
